title: Viscid spider-thread coating breaks into beads at the cylinder stability limit

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Viscid spider-thread coating breaks into beads at the cylinder stability limit

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The sticky fluid coating of a spider's spiral thread, being a liquid cylinder, becomes unstable when its length exceeds its circumference and breaks up into equal, equally spaced beads (often with smaller beads between), the spacing being somewhat greater than theory owing to viscosity and drag on the core thread.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: liquid cylinder of radius r unstable for length l > 2\pi r; breaks into equal, equally spaced beads

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. V: The Forms of Cells

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But this liquid cylinder has its limit of stability when its length equals its own circumference, and therefore just at the points so defined it tends to disrupt into separate segments

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter V, “The Forms of Cells”; topic “Instability of liquid cylinders and beading”. Scope: viscid capture threads of orb-weaving spiders; liquid films on fibres

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: liquid cylinder of radius r unstable for length l > 2\pi r; breaks into equal, equally spaced beads

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch05-12: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The instability threshold and spacing are quantitative and distinguish the capillary model from arbitrary beading. Existing open microscopy can test the geometry in subsets, but matched rheology and formation movies are sparse.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: From calibrated orb-web images, measure coating radius, instability wavelength, bead spacing and size hierarchy, then compare them with Rayleigh-Plateau predictions for a viscous coating on a fiber. Support requires onset near the stated circumference criterion and systematic spacing shifts predicted by viscosity and core drag.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Spider chemistry and active spinning introduce additional controls.

Public images may omit fluid radius, viscosity, or time of formation.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.9
operationalizability: 0.95
data adequacy: 0.45
data existence: 0.6
analysis feasibility: 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The instability criterion and the expected spacing are quantitative and distinguish this account from an arbitrary glue pattern. The measurements exist as published micrographs and would have to be compiled. They are too narrow taxonomically, and too entangled with viscosity and the core fibre, for a definitive test across orb-weavers, but they are enough for a partial one.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On viscid spider capture threads, measure coating radius, bead spacing and bead-size alternation, and compare spacing with the circumference instability threshold and the Rayleigh wavelength. Spacing a little longer than the inviscid prediction, with equal primary beads, would support the claim; a spacing unrelated to cylinder radius, or beads that do not form at that threshold, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Micrographs are concentrated on a few orb-weaver species and often illustrate rather than sample the thread.

No public morphometric table of bead spacing exists.

The axial fibre and glue viscosity both shift the ideal wavelength.
